Part of the course to maturity in Christ is the path wherein we must walk amongst thorns and brambles, and not be swayed.

This path will often come in the form of a challenge where we pull away,k triggered or hurt or struggling with the flaws and faults in others, in our community, church, or organization.

It's a difficult time, but one in which God is actually asking us to grow up and mature. And, to do this, we have to go through that heart-wrenching path where we struggle with faith, belief, difficult questions and feelings about ourselves and others.

Therefore, do not be discouraged by this. It's natural, and a critical part of maturing your faith in Him.

There are three levels of faith, and three levels of obedience.

The first is a child's faith, and a child's obedience. It is so-called blind faith, unquestioning, pure trusting. That heart and faith is the basis of our walking the path. Many are knocked out from coming to God because their child-like faith was violated, and they cannot even get started.

To mature, we must go to the next stage. An adolescent faith, and an adolescent obedience. Adolescence is where our critical faculty kicks in, and we start questioning about everything: what is this? Are my parent perfect? Why do I exist? Why did God create me? etc. Spiritual adolescence is where we encounter difficult questions about yourself, God, and the path.

At this stage, we can do one of three things. One, we can grapple, struggle with those questions, and grow through the adolescent stage. If we hang on, fight and do this, we will reach the next stage. Two, we can abandon the path, avoid the questions, become discouraged, come to disbelieve in God, disgruntled with God, reject God. Three, we can simply avoid the difficult challenges in our heart, without selves and others, and remain as little children. But this is not good. A child's faith is right for a child, but unless we grow, our faith will distort into blind faith, unreasoning faith, ignorant faith.

If we make it through the thorny path of spiritual adolescence, we encounter mature faith. Adult faith, and adult obedience.

A child's faith is faith without questioning, an adolescent's faith is faith while questioning and struggling with those questions. A mature faith, and adult's faith, is faith with understanding, when we understand the Father';s love for us, and know it surely.

One of the first things we encounter in the adolescent stage is fear. Fear that I have done wrong, and God does not love me. Fear that my sion will take me down. Fear that I am not lovable, and that somehow, I might now be seen as worthy.

That fear is a like a terrifying monster who comes to attack us. Like Jacob at the Ford of Jabbok, we must struggle with that fear, and overcome, no matter how long it takes.

When we mature into adult faith, our belief that God loves us is replaced by the experience that God loves us. We come to see our own faults, flaws, and sins, yet, we understand that to God, these are not what he sees. We know he loves us, we experience his love as knowledge, not mere belief.

This is mature faith, belief upheld by knowledge.

The fact that you feel worried says to me, you are encountering this stage of adolescent faith. in the end, we each need to build a relationship with God that stands simply between us, and him, not based on a church, community, or even our action. The fact that you left church says to me that you began to grapple with the difficult issues. Hey, it is hard to love people who may be phoney.
